narrative.title: Spreading Calibration Probes Along a Rail
narrative.scenario: A QA rig places m sensor probes on slots fixed along a straight rail so that the two closest probes end up as far apart as possible - closer spacing causes interference. Slots are given in arbitrary order. Choose the placement that maximizes that minimum spacing and report the spacing achieved.
narrative.inputFormat: An array position of n slot coordinates and an integer m, the number of probes to place.
narrative.outputFormat: The largest possible value of the minimum distance between any two probes.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n log n) (sorting) plus O(n log D) for the search over distances

testCases.explanation: Probes at slots 1, 4 and 7 space every pair at least 3 apart, and no placement beats that.
Placing at 1, 4 and 8 keeps the tightest pair 3 apart; demanding 4 strands the third probe.

hintLevels: Level 1: The question 'can m probes fit with at least d spacing' gets harder as d grows, which is the monotonic shape to exploit.
Level 2: Sort the slots, then for a candidate spacing greedily place probes left to right, each at the first slot at least d beyond the last placement.
Level 3: The search runs from 1 up to the span between the extreme slots, and feasibility should push the bound upward on success because a larger spacing may still fit.
